What was built (CRON_RUN_NOW_ENABLED, strict literal "true", default off):
- capability-core: `InsertFire` and an exported `DueSchedule` view were extracted from `fireOne`. Statements, arguments and order are unchanged, and `fireOne` calls `InsertFire` with the slot key.
- capability-core: new `cron.RunNow`. It runs as one transaction under a `FOR UPDATE` row lock and checks, in order: 400 `invalid_request_id`, 404 `not_found`, 403 `run_now_not_creator`, 409 `approval_expired`, 409 `invalid_schedule`. It then looks up `manual:<request_id>` and returns 200 with `deduplicated:true` if it already exists. Next come 409 `run_now_in_flight` (pending or running and under 15 minutes old) and 429 `run_now_rate_limited` (6 per rolling hour). Then it calls Control `AuthorizeFire`; on refusal it writes a failed fire, commits, returns 403 `fire_not_authorized` and does not disable the schedule. On success it calls `InsertFire`. `next_fire_at` and `last_fire_at` are never touched.
- `CronHandler.WithRunNow(db, authorizer, enabled)` mounts POST `{id}/run` (202 `{data}`; typed errors `{error:{code,message,details:{}}}`). When off, the path falls through to the old routes and returns 404, as before.
- The list gains `features.run_now` and per-row `last_fire_status`/`last_outcome` (LATERAL join), plus a `creator=self` filter that compares against the verified actor.
- `main.go` now builds the fire authorizer before the handler.
- model-gateway: `/v1/cron/:id/run` proxy forwards only `request_id`, and refuses an id that is not URL-safe with a typed 400. `CronListQuery.creator` forwards only the literal `self`.
- BFF: `/api/v1/cron/{cron_id}/run` reads the schedule and allows the creator only, with no admin short-circuit. It forwards only `{request_id}`.
- Frontend: `runScheduleNow` and the new list fields and features in `cron-client.ts`; `schedule.run_now` contract (model plane, risk high).

Following the hard rule, I added no zdr-posture-matrix row. The design's `scheduled_run_now` row would be a feature refusal that duplicates an existing input row. ZDR is refused at the model-gateway (`require_non_zdr_durable_mutation` via `proxy_to_capability_core`), at the capability-core router (`authz.go`) and at the dispatcher.

Tests are written but not run.

The worktree was NOT cut from model-plane. Its HEAD was 21d636a5a (fix/ui-premium-restore), and model-plane (cdfeb5d27) is not an ancestor of it. My owned file domains/spaces.rs does not exist on model-plane, where the code is in domains/spaces/mod.rs. So I wrote model-plane's blobs of the edited files into the worktree with `git show model-plane:<path>`, edited them, staged them with `git add -A`, and wrote the patch with `git diff --cached --binary model-plane -- <3 paths>`. The patch is 867 lines, 777 insertions and 4 deletions, at .plan-work/execution/patches/W3-13/EP-6-S9.patch. It applies to model-plane blobs. The plain `git diff --cached` would have carried the whole branch difference. Nothing was compiled or run.

What I built:
- BFF (spaces/mod.rs):
  - The five pin fields (`agent_ref`, `agent_version`, `agent_digest`, `agent_tool_capability_ids`, `agent_autonomy_cap`) are removed from every turn, whatever the flag says.
  - The binding projection now maps `pinnedVersion` to `pinned_version`.
  - With `state.space_features.agent_version_pinning` on, the turn takes the binding's pinned version (via `agents:getVersionForGateway`), or else the published one (via `agentPersonaForGateway`). It injects that version's instructions and the five fields. If the version cannot be read, the turn is refused with 503 `agent_version_unavailable`; there is no best-effort fallback. With the flag off, the persona injection runs unchanged.
- MG (`http_routes.rs` `InvokeRequest`): five `serde(default)` raw-JSON fields, the same idiom as `agent_roles`, so request parsing is byte-identical.
- MG (`sse.rs`), behind new switch `MODEL_GATEWAY_AGENT_TOOL_ALLOWLIST` (strict, only literal "true"):
  - `agent_pin()` validates the pin strictly; a malformed pin is refused with `agent_pin_invalid`, never dropped.
  - `narrow_to_agent_allowlist()` only removes. MG has no tool-name-to-capability binding (that is execution-core's `trusted_capability_id`). So an Ask turn with an allowlist loses its client tools, the `tools` feature and `browse_web`. A Do or execute turn with an allowlist is refused with `agent_tool_allowlist_do_unsupported`.
  - `resolve_turn_with_agent_cap()` adds the cap to the WS25-S6 resolve as `Ceiling{source:"agent"}`. It is the same as before when the cap is absent or auto.
  - The pin's ids and digest go to a log line; the instructions never do.
- Tests written, not run: 4 BFF tokio tests (pinned v2 after v3 publish, unpinned follows published, unreadable pin refused, forged fields stripped with the flag off, on, and with no mention) and 11 MG unit tests.

- zdr-posture-matrix.json is unchanged: there is no new resolver input and no metadata write.

With the switch on, an Ask turn with an allowlist loses every tool and a Do turn with one is refused, because only execution-core maps tool names to capability ids; a real intersection needs `RunAgentRequest` field 26 plus enforcement in execution-core.

Other BFF routes that forward bodies to MG `/v1/invoke` (for example agent_api) do not strip the five pin fields; a forged pin can only narrow the turn but can mislabel the pin log line, so those routes should strip them too.

The pinned or published version is not checked against the Space's binding beyond the existing roster join, and a cross-org pinned version reads as null and is refused; a live proof (design F5) should show that MG logs `agent_version=1` after v2 is published.

What was built:
- **capability-core list:** the list now returns `{"policies":[...],"enforced":bool}` instead of a bare array. A `data` envelope was not usable because the SPA's `unwrap()` would drop the bit. The value comes from a new `ToolPoliciesHandler.WithEnforced`. Left unset it reports false, so nothing is shown as enforced by mistake.
- **capability-core set:** `set` refuses `ask` on `cap.tool.provider.execute` with 422 `already_always_ask`, for both user and org scope. ask/never on `cap.tool.provider.read` and never on execute were already accepted; allow on either is still refused because both are built-in kind `tool`.
- **Go tests:** I updated `tool_policies_integration_test.go` (beside the owned file) to the new list shape.
- **model-gateway:** `connector_reads.rs` gains `ReadPolicy` (`Unrestricted` / `AskFirst` / `Off` / `Unknown`), the pure `policy_of`, `fetch_policy` (GET `/api/v1/tool-policies?capability_id=cap.tool.provider.read` with the person's capability bearer) and `read_policy`. `read_policy` keeps a 60 s cache per (org, user), capped at 4096 entries; an unknown answer is not cached. When enforcement is off the result is always `Unrestricted`. The gateway's existing `connector_turn.filter(connector_offered)` already makes `read_outcome` refuse once the read is not offered.
- **execution-core:** test-only change. The mock gets an optional `policy_source`, plus tests `user_ask_on_provider_read_pauses`, `user_never_on_provider_read_denies` and `user_never_on_provider_execute_denies`, run under the Shadow and Enforce gates.
- **SPA contracts:** `integrations.list_connector_policies` and `integrations.set_connector_policy` (owner plane model, risk low, reversible, not executable by the model). `set_connector_policy` takes a discriminated union of read levels {use_without_asking, ask_first, off} and write levels {always_ask, off}.
- **SPA client:** `orchestration-client.ts` adds `connectorPoliciesOf`, `listConnectorPolicies`, `connectorPolicyRequest` and `setConnectorPolicy`. Returning to the default level revokes the user row; a 404 on that revoke counts as success.
- **Settings panel:** confirmed the mount point is `IntegrationsSection` in `WorkspaceSettingsPage.tsx`. `ConnectedAppsPolicy` is mounted after the integrations list. It shows "Not enforced yet" while enforcement is off, a note when the org's level is stricter, and the Ask-first / Do-mode note.

depth_findings.text: Pre-existing: the Do loop's `_browser_release` guard (RunRelease::drop) closes the run's Quarry page whenever a request returns paused, so any approval pause (e.g. browser.act BrowserActionRisk) loses the page before its release; S1 only exempts takeover pauses through the in-process hold set.

The browser session and the takeover hold live in one execution-core process's memory, so a give-back that resumes on another replica (or after a restart) finds no session and the released call answers browser_not_open; a hold whose approval expires is never cleared, and the Quarry run lives on until its grant TTL (30 min) or Quarry's idle sweep (S5 territory).
A takeover pause needs the loop-owned resume (WS03 continue/loop-resume switches on): with continuation mode cold the delivery worker would try to run browser.observe/open, which it cannot serve.

Verify live that execution-core's browser:execute service token may read GET /v1/agent/runs/{id}/browser-session on its own runs, and that the read's `live.touch()` does not keep a held run from Quarry's idle sweep in a way Q-5 does not expect.

If Quarry's control cannot be read, `open_with` and `released_browser_call_still_held` let the call through (fail-open). The guarantee that the agent never acts during a takeover then rests on QUARRY_EDGE__TAKEOVER_ENFORCEMENT=1 (Q-4).

The paused event's control_epoch is read from Quarry's projection after the pause, not from the USER_TOOK_OVER details.control_epoch. The refusal reaches the loop as text only, so the event can carry a later epoch if the person flips quickly.

Loop-level behaviour has no unit test that drives run_rounds: a refused call becoming a pause, the hold being set, and Paused/Resumed being published. The browser_session tests cover the parts; the rest needs an agent.rs run_rounds test with a Quarry stub.

The design's live proof (take over, refused agent call, card, BrowserRunPaused, give back with epoch 2, approval consumed once, run completes; second user 404; stale epoch 409) waits on Q-1, Q-4, WS21-S5a open working live, and the WS21-S6 binding.
